synopsis: Domain randomization varies simulated appearance and scene conditions to reduce dependence on details that differ in reality; the booklet presents it as a way to improve machine-learning perception robustness, not as functional safety evidence [f13585, f13586, f13594]. A vendor-labelled 2026 overview describes Isaac Sim Replicator randomizing pose, scale, lighting and materials, while a 2022 construction study provides an excavator-pose estimation example [f3791, f4135, f13588]. Its benefits have limits: a 2026 study found that Unity-rendered construction scenes still diverged from real photometric distributions despite extensive randomization, and the glossary reports a persistent synthetic-only training gap while noting that mixing real and synthetic images helps [f10584, f13590, f13589]. Randomized appearance does not establish correct radar physics or braking distance, and no peer-reviewed demonstration was found that synthetic-only training or validation establishes collision-avoidance reliability for heavy off-road machines [f13592, f13591]. Randomized simulation runs must freeze their random seeds for reproducibility [f13593].
